source.title: What's in a Loss Function for Image Classification?
source.authors: Simon Kornblith; Honglak Lee; Ting Chen; Mohammad Norouzi

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests dropout’s effect on held-out image-classification accuracy using a different ImageNet setup; it does not test the claim’s random-label, architecture-width, optimizer, batch-size, or sharpness comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper compares nine training objectives and reports ImageNet training and validation accuracy, transfer accuracy, and representation measurements. Only the dropout results bear directly on V6. Cited findings about other studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out image-classification accuracy with and without penultimate-layer dropout in ImageNet-trained ResNet-50 and Inception v3 models, testing V6 in additional architecture and dataset settings. It is not an original source for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: objectives including dropout improve ImageNet accuracy but generally reduce fixed-feature transferability, while the pretraining objective has little effect after full fine-tuning. The authors associate this trade-off with increased class separation and representation changes concentrated in later layers.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares tuned image-classification objectives on ImageNet rather than the original dropout study’s range of datasets and model settings; its dropout is applied to the penultimate layer of ResNet-50.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with the training objective and, for cosine softmax, temperature; the paper also reports dataset-specific transfer differences. These do not establish dropout’s small-dataset behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout-pretrained fixed features transfer worse on most downstream datasets, while full fine-tuning largely removes differences between pretraining objectives.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Improving ImageNet accuracy through output-layer regularization can reduce fixed-feature transfer performance without materially changing fully fine-tuned performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Class separation increases with alternative objectives and correlates negatively with fixed-feature transfer accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Penultimate-layer class separation predicts transferability across these ImageNet training objectives.

record.peer_reviewed: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021)
record.problems: The dropout effect is measured in one main architecture and pretraining dataset. The text does not report a small-training-set dropout comparison; training accuracy is reported separately from validation accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted under the 60-row limit. Other losses’ validation and training accuracies describe objective comparisons but do not measure dropout’s effect; fixed-feature transfer and representation measurements concern outcomes outside the V6 claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: Inception v3 dropout comparison: validation top-1 accuracy 79.0% versus 78.6% for softmax; top-5 accuracy 94.50% versus 94.24%, averaged over three pretraining initializations.

ResNet-50 dropout versus softmax on distribution-shift benchmarks: V2 accuracy 65.4 versus 65.0%; A 3.1 versus 2.7%; Sketch 23.0 versus 21.8%; R 37.2 versus 36.8%; C mean corruption error 74.5 versus 75.9, where lower is better. Results average eight models per objective.

record.verdict_notes: Transfer results do not challenge V6's within-task held-out accuracy claim. Table C.4 reports maximum holdout accuracies used during tuning, so its dropout combinations should not be added as independent test-result rows. The study contains no relevant random-label, width, architecture-type, optimizer, batch-size, sharpness, or memorized-example removal comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning.
Small training sets, fully connected classifiers, dropout rates that underfit, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap; class separation measurements are not this version’s measure.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

conditions.value: penultimate layer; keep probability hyperparameter tuned

rows.uncertainty: Table 1 values averaged over 8 pretraining runs; no uncertainty value shown there. Text says the tested objectives except squared error significantly improve over softmax (p < 0.05).
rows.locator: Section 3.1, Table 1; Appendix C.1, Table C.1
rows.note: Dropout validation accuracy is 0.5 percentage points higher than softmax; the paper reports significance for the group of tested objectives except squared error.
rows.check: The accuracy values are correct. Table 3 supplies uncertainty: dropout 77.5 ± 0.04% versus softmax 77.0 ± 0.06%. Add independently selected training durations: dropout 172 epochs versus softmax 146 epochs (Table A.1); this is a comparison of tuned recipes.
